title: How the Monthly Premium on a Medicare Supplement Policy Is Built
content:
The premium on a policy under Medicare Supplement Insurance Policies is built from the plan letter's base monthly premium for a standard policyholder issued at 65, adjusted for the rating method the letter uses, the policyholder's rating class and area, and then reduced by whichever discounts they qualify for.

### Age

On an issue-age letter the base premium rises by the issue-age step for each year of age above 65 at issue and never rises again with age; on an attained-age letter it rises by the attained-age increase at each policy anniversary.

### The rating factors and the fee

The tobacco factor and the area factor multiply the base premium before any discount is taken, and the annual policy fee is added afterwards and is never discounted.

### The discounts

The household discount and the annual payment discount stack: both are taken, one after the other, on the premium after the rating factors and before the policy fee.

### The order stated as a sequence of quantities

The rated monthly premium is the plan letter's base monthly premium at 65 multiplied by the letter's tobacco factor and by its area factor, rounded to the cent. The discounted monthly premium is that rated monthly premium less the letter's household discount taken on it, rounded to the cent. The amount charged is that discounted monthly premium together with the monthly share of the annual policy fee, that share being the letter's annual policy fee spread over the twelve months of the policy year and rounded to the cent.

Because the two rating factors act on the base premium before any discount, and the fee is added after every discount, a discount never touches the fee and a factor never acts on a discounted figure.

### Rate increases

An across-the-board rate increase is applied in the plan letter's annual rate review month and only after the policyholder has had the letter's notice days of written warning; a rate increase is never applied retrospectively to a period already billed.

### Why the bill shows several entries

Each rate component is posted as its own ledger entry, so that a policyholder asking why their bill changed can be shown the base premium, the increase and the fee separately rather than one figure.
